transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep getting hit with these memories out of nowhere. It’s like I’m back seeing my cousin on the pavement — I can hear the shouting and see the lights again, even when I’m just standing in the church office trying to act normal.
What seems to trigger these memories?

It can be almost nothing. I’ll just be standing in the church office, trying to get through the day, and suddenly I’m seeing my cousin on the pavement again. The shouting, the lights — it all comes back like I’m right there.
Do you find yourself avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened to your cousin?

Yeah. I go out of my way to avoid certain spots. I’ll take the long way around town just so I don’t have to pass the community center or that court. And if someone starts bringing up that night, I usually cut it off or make up a reason to leave.
Do you have trouble sleeping or find yourself feeling constantly on edge?

Yeah, I’m on edge a lot. I can’t sit with my back to a door anymore. At church events, instead of really listening to people, I’m watching their hands, checking corners, noticing cars slowing down outside, and keeping track of where the nearest exit is. It’s exhausting.
Do you try to avoid thinking about what happened to your cousin?

Yes. I try not to let myself go there. I’ll avoid places that bring it back, like I’ll take the long way around so I don’t pass the community center or that court. And if someone starts talking about that night, I usually shut it down or find some reason to leave.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when these memories come back?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed it like that, like watching myself from outside my body. When the memories come back, I just feel caught up in them, but I don’t know if I’d describe it that way.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you when these memories come back?

Yeah… I do. It’s like even when I’m around people at church, people calling me “brother” or asking me to pray with them, I still feel far away. Like I’m behind glass or something, and nobody can really reach me.
Do you often think that you're a bad person or that you're to blame for what happened to your cousin?

Yes. I keep going over it and thinking it was my fault. Like if I had ended things sooner, or walked him out myself, or just kept a better eye on those boys… maybe my cousin would still be here. I know people tell me I couldn’t have known, but it doesn’t feel that way.
Do you often wish you could undo what happened or punish yourself in some way for what you think you could have done differently to prevent your cousin's death?

Yeah. I keep wishing I could go back and do it different. I tell myself if I had ended the event earlier, or walked him out myself, or paid closer attention to those boys, maybe my cousin would still be alive. It’s hard not to feel like I should’ve done something.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy before your cousin's death?

Yeah. I used to really love preaching, playing keys, taking pictures, even running with the guys on the court. Now… I either avoid it or I just do it because I’m supposed to. It doesn’t feel alive in me like it used to.
Are there any activities that you still find yourself enjoying as much as you did before your cousin's death?

Not really. The things I used to enjoy—preaching, playing keys, taking pictures, even playing ball with the guys—I either avoid them now or just do them because I have to. It feels like I’m just going through the motions. None of it feels the same anymore.
How long have you been experiencing these memories and feelings since your cousin's death?
It’s been going on since he was killed… about two years and three months now.
How often do you think about your cousin's death being your fault in a typical day?

A lot. Probably more times than I can count in a day. I keep going back over it, thinking if I had ended things earlier, or walked him out, or just kept a better watch over those boys… maybe my cousin would still be here.
Do you think about your cousin's death being your fault every hour of the day?

Yeah… pretty much. Maybe not literally every single minute, but it comes up constantly. I keep telling myself if I had ended the event earlier, or walked him out, or watched those boys better, my cousin would still be here.
Are there any days where you don't think about your cousin's death at all?
No… not really. I can’t think of a day where it doesn’t come up. I keep blaming myself, thinking if I’d ended the event earlier, walked him out, or watched those boys better, he might still be here.
